newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME zinc seen trying US$1,500, copper seen easier.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc seen trying US$1,500, copper seen easier.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc prices are seen mounting a challenge to the key US$1,500 a tonne resistance level later on Friday before retreating, dealers said.
"I have a feeling zinc will touch $1,500 today, but then it's going to be a good sell," one dealer said.
"Zinc should test $1,500 but then you'll see profit-taking come in and it will fail to hold at that level. But it will definitely be above $1,500 next week."

Metal brokers Brandeis said in its daily review that three-month zinc finished positively on the LME on Thursday, ending $15 up on the day at $1,479 a tonne. Regional dealers quoted three-month metal at around $1,480/85 at 0300 GMT.
Broker Rudolf Wolff said its daily report that it is looking for zinc to finish above its recent high of $1,495 in order "to suggest an initial target of $1,530 (a tonne)."
Copper prices, on the other hand, are tipped to open slightly easier on the LME and should consolidate at current levels before trying to surmount resistance at $2,300 a tonne, dealers said.
"Copper should drop a bit," a senior Japanese dealer said.
"It (copper) should struggle on the upside," another trader said. "It really depends on what the funds will do."
Rudolf Wolff said copper would need to conslidate "before re-challenging overhead resistance."
"The market needs to breach $2,300, however, to move higher and will then look to fill the gap between $2,365 and $2,308," Brandeis said.
Three-month copper was quoted by the trade at 0300 GMT at around $2,283/88 a tonne, slightly down from the late quote on the LME of $2,290 a tonne.
Cash copper was seen at $2,380 a tonne with the backwardation pegged at around $110-$120.
